summary: Paraguay's foreign ministry lists the countries whose nationals do not need a visa, among them the EU states, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, and says that anyone whose country is not listed does need one. The Dirección Nacional de Migraciones admits non-resident foreigners for a maximum of 90 days, extendable once, and accepts the national identity document of Mercosur and associated-country citizens as a travel document. Visa applications are made through the foreign ministry's online form, followed by an interview, and nationals of Qatar and Oman are granted a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Paraguay. The Government of Canada says Paraguay experiences extreme dry periods between April and September and that the rainy season extends from December to March, when the eastern part of the country is more at risk of floods; it says seasonal flooding can make roads impassable, particularly in the Chaco region, and that bush and forest fires are common between mid-July and December, particularly in Concepción, Amambay, San Pedro and Canindeyú.

idp.text: The UN treaty records list Paraguay as a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (accession, 18 October 1965). Paraguay's National Traffic and Road Safety Law (Law No. 5016, art. 27), as published by the Library and Archive of the National Congress, says a driving licence issued abroad is valid in Paraguay for no more than three months from entry into the country; it must be current, and it allows driving cars of the category the licence authorises. The UK government says a UK photocard driving licence can be used to drive in Paraguay and that you need your driving licence and your passport showing the entry stamp with you in the car; Canada's travel advice says you must carry an international driving permit. Both governments say the legal blood alcohol limit is 0.00%. No official source we could read states Paraguay's own rule on whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Paraguay?
faq.answer: Not if your country is on the foreign ministry's list of countries whose nationals do not need a visa; it includes the EU states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and Israel, and the ministry says that if your country is not listed you do need a visa. The Dirección Nacional de Migraciones admits non-resident foreigners for a maximum of 90 days and accepts the national identity document of Mercosur and associated-country citizens as a travel document. Visa applications are made through the foreign ministry's online form, and nationals of Qatar and Oman are granted a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Paraguay?
faq.answer: No. Paraguay's Consulate General in New York says Law 7314/2024, which extends Law 6790/2021 for three additional years, eliminates visa requirements for citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand who wish to enter Paraguay for tourism, provided their stay does not exceed 90 days, until 13 August 2027.

faq.question: Can I enter Paraguay with a national ID card instead of a passport?
faq.answer: The Dirección Nacional de Migraciones says the national identity document of the country of origin is a valid travel document exclusively for Mercosur citizens travelling to another member or associated country of the bloc, and lists Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Peru, Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador.

faq.question: Is there a Paraguayan eVisa?
faq.answer: No official page we read describes an electronic visa. Paraguay's Consulate General in New York says visa applications are made through the foreign ministry's online form (mre.gov.py/visasenlinea), after which the consulate contacts you to schedule an interview. It also says nationals of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Qatar, Oman and Taiwan are granted a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport on presentation of a valid passport.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 90 days in Paraguay?
faq.answer: The Dirección Nacional de Migraciones admits non-resident foreigners for a maximum of 90 days, extendable once at the person's request for no longer than the period first granted, at its discretion. The fee is Gs. 557,510.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Paraguay?
faq.answer: Paraguay's health ministry requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate from everyone aged 1 to 59 travelling from or to the risk zones it lists: Bolivia (Santa Cruz), Brazil (Amazonas, Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Rio Grande do Sul and Roraima), Colombia (Caquetá, Huila, Nariño, Putumayo, Vaupés and Tolima), Guyana (Boa Vista and Siparuni) and Peru (Huánuco, Junín, Madre de Dios, San Martín and Ucayali).

tips.border-stamps.text: Make sure that an immigration official stamps, dates and signs your passport when you arrive. If you do not have an entry stamp in your passport, you will get a fine when you leave the country.

This is important if you enter Paraguay at a land border, typically the crossing between Ciudad del Este and Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil. Long-distance bus drivers sometimes tell foreign nationals that they can complete immigration formalities in Asunción. This is not true, and you will get a fine if you do not get your passport stamped at the point of entry.

countryFacts.safety.text: Transnational criminal organisations carry out drug trafficking and arms smuggling along Paraguay’s eastern border with Brazil. Most activity is from Pedro Juan Caballero south to Ciudad del Este, and to the Tri-Border Area where the borders of Paraguay, Brazil and Argentina meet.

Violent crime is on the increase in this area – take particular care in the departments (‘departamentos’) that border Brazil: Amambay Department Concepción Department Alto Paraná Department San Pedro Department Canindeyú Department
A small guerrilla-style group calling itself the Ejercito del Pueblo Paraguayo (EPP) operates in the north of the Department of San Pedro and the south of the Department of Concepción.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: Paraguay experiences extreme dry periods between April and September.
